extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media professionals, policymakers, researchers and students interested in the Canadian news market
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level profile summarizing the state of the Canadian news ecosystem: audience behaviours, platform impact, business models, trust and press freedom, and policy interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population
rubrics_metrics.description: Population: 38 million

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet penetration: 94%

rubrics_metrics.name: High consumption of foreign news sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Canada is a bilingual market with high consumption of news from foreign sources, especially the USA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for local publishers: competition from large foreign brands (e.g., CNN, Apple News, New York Times) for Canadian audiences and subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform visibility and policy impact (Online News Act & Meta response)
rubrics_metrics.description: News content is no longer visible on Meta’s social media platforms in response to the Online News Act which required tech companies to compensate news organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences cited include protests (blank front pages), advertisers withdrawing business from Meta, and reduced visibility for news publishers — especially hurting local and regional outlets that relied on Facebook traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic and sharing trend on social platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall traffic to Facebook is largely unaffected, though news consumption and sharing is down 15 percentage points in the past two years, at its lowest level since the Reuters Institute survey began.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an indicator of how platform policy and audience behaviour affect distribution and reach of news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift of news consumption to other platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: News consumption on other networks such as YouTube and TikTok is up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track emerging platform usage as both an audience opportunity and a redistribution of traffic away from legacy social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation criteria for government/tech-company funding (Google deal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the money from the Google deal will go to broadcasters (including public media) and the bulk of money is to be distributed among eligible organisations based on the number of journalists employed, allocated by a collective body which will settle disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes an explicit quantitative eligibility/allocation metric (journalist headcount) for distributing platform compensation funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription growth and competitive landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Big national brands like the National Post and Globe and Mail have been building subscription numbers but face competition (free and paid) from US-based news brands which have signed up Canadian news consumers in large numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure publishers by subscription growth while accounting for cross-border competition from international news brands for the same paying audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and structural pressures on local and hyperlocal news
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic and structural pressures contributed to the reduction or closure of hundreds of local and hyperlocal news services; major groups (e.g., Bell Canada Enterprises, Québecor) eliminated thousands of jobs and closed or sold stations/publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use layoffs, closures, sales, and creditor protection filings as indicators of local news ecosystem health and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of changes to delivery infrastructure (end of door-to-door flyer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of a door-to-door flyer delivery service in Ontario and Quebec forced dozens of community newspapers to become digital only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution infrastructure changes can be a proximate cause of business-model shifts (print→digital) for community newspapers; track these structural changes when evaluating local news viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-born local aggregation business model (Village Media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Village Media’s model of bundling local information such as weather, classified ads, school bus schedules, and community webcams has allowed the company to expand its network across Ontario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a sustainability criterion, evaluate whether a publisher bundles local services and utility content to build audience and revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversified revenue approaches: boutique ads and donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital French-language daily La Presse saw growth thanks to its boutique ad service (asks readers to volunteer information through quizzes) and had a successful donation drive; Le Devoir increased digital subscriptions by 13% and is registered to issue tax receipts to donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess publishers' use of diversified revenue (targeted ad services, donations, subscription offers, tax-receipting) as indicators of financial resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology partnerships for classifieds and obituary hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: AdPerfect partnered with Torstar for technology to host obituaries; AdPerfect was acquired by Tribute Technology, a leading software provider to funeral homes in North America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how publishers outsource or partner for classifieds/obituary platforms and what acquisitions/partnerships imply for local publishing infrastructure and revenue streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public support and tax incentives for journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Local Journalism Initiative (a subsidy programme) has been renewed, the cap on expenditures for the journalism labour tax credit is set to be increased, and some provincial and municipal governments are contributing to support news organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track public subsidy programmes, tax credits, and government ad spending commitments as structural supports that affect newsroom resourcing and survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI in journalism and preliminary guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Amid concerns about misinformation produced with generative AI, organisations such as the Globe and Mail, La Presse, and CBC made public their preliminary guidelines for the use of AI; tools are being incorporated into workflows (automating checking of content, AI-produced transcripts and text summaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate editorial policy and operational use of AI (existence of guidelines, specific use-cases like transcription or automated fact-checking) as part of journalistic quality and risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for online news (willingness to pay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay for online news: 15% overall; English-speaking: 16%; French-speaking: 11%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these proportions as a baseline for measuring propensity to pay and subscription market potential in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to podcasts (audience engagement metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to podcast in the last month: 41% overall; English-speaking: 44%; French-speaking: 29%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Podcast reach is an engagement indicator and potential revenue/extension channel for publishers to evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news overall
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in news overall: 39% (noted as a downward trend with a loss of almost 20 percentage points since 2018); trust has fallen equally among English- and French-speaking markets, though trust for most individual brands has risen a little among those familiar with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use overall trust levels and trends, plus brand-specific trust among familiar audiences, as indicators of credibility and audience confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press freedom ranking (RSF World Press Freedom Index)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF World Press Freedom Index: 14/180, Score 81.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include international press freedom rankings and scores when assessing the broader operating environment for journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall audience engagement and revenue difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging broad audiences online and generating revenue is increasingly difficult, especially for local and regional news outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative descriptions of engagement/revenue challenges alongside quantitative metrics to evaluate sustainability and strategic needs of news organisations.
